source.title: Generalisation error in learning with random features and the hidden manifold model
source.authors: Federica Gerace; Bruno Loureiro; Florent Krzakala; M. M'ezard; Lenka Zdeborov'a

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the relevant findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes test error as feature count crosses the interpolation threshold using random-feature linear models, a different method and setting from the one-hidden-layer ReLU experiments in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper studies synthetic teacher-generated labels, not random-label memorization. It does not test whether a network that fits random labels generalizes on natural labels. Its own feature-count sweeps bear on V2; the many cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V2's post-interpolation generalization pattern using random-feature networks with fixed first-layer weights and analytically optimized readouts on synthetic classification data. This differs from training all weights of ReLU networks on images.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive a replica-based asymptotic generalization formula, demonstrate logistic double descent with a peak at linear separability, and report close numerical agreement. The formula remains conjectural beyond special cases with existing rigorous results.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes regularized generalized linear models with random features and synthetic teacher-generated data, rather than training the specified ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10. It includes ridge regularization and uses theory plus gradient-descent simulations.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature count and loss change the interpolation-peak location; regularization changes the plotted error and peak behavior. Orthogonal versus Gaussian projections also change generalization error, but that comparison does not measure V2's width claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonal projections outperform Gaussian projections and reach the kernel limit with fewer features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured orthogonal feature maps can improve generalization and feature efficiency relative to Gaussian feature maps.

fits_no_version.finding: Hidden-manifold classification generalizes better when latent dimension is small relative to sample count and ambient dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent data structure affects generalization in overparameterized random-feature classifiers.

record.problems: The main predictions rely on a non-rigorous replica calculation. The authors say a rigorous proof remains open beyond a particular special case. Numerical results use synthetic data, and the relevant plotted curve values are not stated in text; uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported comparisons of orthogonal and Gaussian projections and hidden-manifold dimension are outside the measured behavior named by the claim versions. Figure-only curve points were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label versus random-label held-out performance using the same architecture and recipe.

Training all weights of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 without explicit regularization. The optimized-regularization rows also do not test continued improvement conditional on zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: The optimally regularized square-loss classification width sweep, including its approximately 0.17 kernel-limit error. R2 records only the small fixed penalty, while R3 records only optimized logistic loss.
missing.locator: Figure 2, blue dashed curve; Section 3.1, kernel-limit comparison

missing.what: The logistic width sweep at λ = 10^-3 with direct simulations on the original and Gaussian-equivalent models, alongside the theoretical prediction. This supplies numerical validation absent from the Figure 2 rows.
The logistic generalization-error surface varying both p/n and n/d, showing that the interpolation threshold changes with sample-to-input dimension ratio.

record.verdict_notes: An interpolation peak alone would not establish V2; the relevant evidence is the subsequent decrease with feature count. Architectural, dataset, and regularization differences delimit what was tested rather than independently demonstrating a failure of V2. No supplied result establishes a challenge to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels in the same architecture and recipe.

One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10, zero training error without explicit regularization, and the specified width sweep. The study instead analyzes random features on synthetic data with ridge regularization; it does not establish behavior for the specified networks or datasets.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image datasets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measures tracking generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: random Gaussian features, logistic classification
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of random Gaussian features per sample and measured generalisation error.
rows.note: The text states that the generalisation-error peak occurs when training loss goes to zero and identifies the logistic peak with linear separability. The figure plots error against p/n; no curve values are given in the text.
rows.check: The partial designation is unwarranted: Section 3.1 reports double descent, including decreasing generalization error beyond interpolation. Figure 2 contains theoretical predictions, not direct simulation measurements. Its nonzero ridge penalty should not be described as an exact unregularized fit.

rows.subject: random Gaussian features, square-loss classification
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of random Gaussian features per sample and measured generalisation error.
rows.note: The text identifies the peak at p/n = 1, where the system of n linear equations with p parameters becomes solvable. The curve values are only shown in the figure.
rows.check: Section 3.1 reports the post-interpolation decrease, with the square-loss peak at p/n = 1. Figure 2 contains theoretical predictions. The small nonzero ridge penalty means exact zero training loss is a limiting interpretation.

rows.subject: random Gaussian features, logistic classification
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of random Gaussian features per sample and measured generalisation error with regularization optimized for each p/n.
rows.note: The text reports the kernel-limit generalisation error at optimal regularisation as approximately 0.16, and says the peak occurs near the logistic interpolation threshold. It does not give the curve's intermediate values.
rows.check: The row bears on the width trend under optimized regularization. Its approximately 0.16 kernel-limit error is explicitly stated in Section 3.1 and should replace the wholly figure-only value description. The lower training-loss panel applies only to fixed λ = 10^-4; it does not establish interpolation for this optimally regularized curve.

source_check.correct: Generalisation error approaches approximately 0.16 as p/n → ∞ for logistic classification with optimal regularisation. Intermediate curve values remain figure-only.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, p. 10, paragraph immediately before Section 3.2; Figure 2 caption.
source_check.problem: The wholly figure-only value description omits the explicitly stated numerical kernel-limit error.
